cases.expected: The method returns the same JsonSchema instance because getParentSchema() returns null (no parent).
cases.description: Verify that a root schema (no parent) returns itself as the ancestor.

cases.expected: The method returns the direct parent JsonSchema instance because the parent’s getParentSchema() returns null.
cases.description: Verify that a schema with a single parent returns that parent as the ancestor.

cases.expected: The method returns the top‑most ancestor (grandparent) JsonSchema instance when the schema has a parent that itself has a parent.
cases.description: Verify recursive traversal: a child schema with a parent and a grandparent returns the grandparent as the ancestor.

cases.expected: The method returns the top‑most ancestor (root) JsonSchema instance when the schema is part of a deep chain (e.g., 5 levels).
cases.description: Create a chain of five JsonSchema objects where each child’s parent points to the previous one. Calling findAncestor() on the deepest child should traverse recursively and return the root (first) schema.

cases.expected: StackOverflowError is thrown due to infinite recursion when a schema’s parent reference points to itself.
cases.description: Set a JsonSchema instance’s parent to itself (schema.setParentSchema(schema)). The recursive implementation has no cycle detection, so findAncestor() should cause a StackOverflowError.

cases.expected: Calling findAncestor() on the result of a previous findAncestor() call returns the same instance (idempotent).
cases.description: For a schema with a parent chain, invoke findAncestor() to obtain the root, then invoke findAncestor() again on that root. The second call should return the same root instance, confirming that the method is idempotent.

cases.expected: After invoking findAncestor(), the original schema’s parent reference remains unchanged.
cases.description: Create a child schema with a known parent. Call findAncestor() on the child and then verify that child.getParentSchema() still returns the original parent, ensuring the method does not mutate state.

cases.expected: IllegalStateException is propagated when getParentSchema() throws it.
cases.description: Create a subclass of JsonSchema that overrides getParentSchema() to throw IllegalStateException. Invoking findAncestor() should not catch the exception, allowing it to bubble up.

cases.expected: StackOverflowError is thrown due to infinite recursion caused by an indirect parent cycle (e.g., A → B → C → A).
cases.description: Construct three JsonSchema instances A, B, and C where A.setParentSchema(B), B.setParentSchema(C), and C.setParentSchema(A). Calling findAncestor() on any of them should trigger unbounded recursion and result in a StackOverflowError.
